name: Jira
verdict: Self-serve: enable sharing under Distribution and anyone with your authorization URL can install, with a warning that Atlassian has not reviewed the app. Since 2026-03-02 API quotas are a points pool shared across tenants.
needGuide: Short one, but read the 2026 points-based quota rules before relying on it at scale.

auth.detail: OAuth 2.0 (3LO) authorization code via auth.atlassian.com; add offline_access for a refresh token. Refresh tokens rotate (each use issues a new one and disables the old; 10-minute reuse window) and expire after 90 days of inactivity. After auth, call /oauth/token/accessible-resources to get the cloudid and use api.atlassian.com/ex/jira/{cloudid}/.... Access token lifetime comes back as expires_in (commonly 1 hour; not stated on the page).

effort.timeToProduction: 1-3 days with sharing only; Marketplace approval timeline unknown

approval.gate: New apps are private (creator only). Turning on Distribution → Enable sharing lets anyone with the authorization URL install, with no review. Users see a warning that Atlassian has not reviewed the integration until it is approved through the Marketplace process. 3LO apps can only have informational Marketplace listings with limited features. Since 2026-03-02, points-based API quotas apply (65,000 points/hour in a global pool shared across all tenants); a per-tenant pool needs Atlassian review via the Partner Portal.

scopes.why: Granular and classic scopes added per API in the console; changing scopes forces re-consent and some resources aren't available to 3LO.
scopes.summary: Granular and classic Jira scopes added per API in the console; request only scopes already added. Changing scopes forces re-consent. Some resources are not available to 3LO at all. offline_access is needed for refresh tokens. No scope documented as triggering review.

cost: Free to build and share; Marketplace listing terms not researched
prerequisites: Account and owner: An Atlassian account in the developer console owns the app; use a company-owned account (ownership transfer not documented).
Where you register: Developer console → Create → OAuth 2.0 integration → Permissions (add Jira API + scopes) → Authorization → OAuth 2.0 (3LO) → Configure callback URL → Distribution → Enable sharing
Cost: Free to build and share; Marketplace listing terms not researched

registerAt.path: Developer console → Create → OAuth 2.0 integration → Permissions (add Jira API + scopes) → Authorization → OAuth 2.0 (3LO) → Configure callback URL → Distribution → Enable sharing

steps.do: Sign in to developer.atlassian.com/console/myapps with a company account and click Create → OAuth 2.0 integration
Under Permissions add Jira platform REST API and the minimum scopes (e.g. read:jira-work, write:jira-work, read:jira-user) plus offline_access in the request
Under Authorization → OAuth 2.0 (3LO) → Configure, set the exact callback URL
Implement code exchange, accessible-resources lookup (cloudid per site), rotating-refresh storage with a lock per user, and points-quota backoff using the RateLimit-Reason header
Under Distribution, complete the sharing form and enable sharing; copy the authorization URL
Test with an account on a separate site, including re-consent after a scope change
Optionally request Marketplace approval to remove the unreviewed warning

roles.team: An Atlassian account in the developer console owns the app; use a company-owned account (ownership transfer not documented).
roles.console: none documented in the pages read (a collaborator or ownership setting may exist in the console; unconfirmed).
roles.customer: The authorizing user picks sites (account-level grant spans sites, resource-level limits to selected ones). Effective access is still limited by the user's Jira permissions. An admin cannot revoke a user's grant from the Connected Apps user screen; they can only uninstall the app. Org-level app access rules not confirmed.

testing: The app is private by default and works for the creator's own sites.
A free Atlassian cloud developer site is the likely test tenant (not confirmed in fetched pages).
Invite a second account on another site to test the sharing link.

blockers.problem: Refresh token reuse or 90 days of inactivity gives invalid_grant
blockers.fix: Store each new refresh token immediately, lock refreshes, and prompt re-auth.
Start Marketplace approval early or brief admins in advance.

blockers.problem: Shared 65,000 points/hour global pool can throttle all customers together
blockers.fix: Cache, batch, and request tier 2 via Partner Portal if usage is large.

blockers.problem: Each site has a different cloudid and users may authorize several sites
blockers.fix: Always key tokens and calls by cloudid.

automation.agentCan: Write the 3LO flow, token storage, cloudid routing, rate-limit handling, Marketplace listing copy, and run test calls against a dev site.
automation.humanMust: Console sign-in and app creation, completing the sharing form with company details, any Marketplace submission, and customer admin communication.

uncertain: The vendor/privacy info required by the Distribution form, Atlassian org-admin app access rules, console collaborator roles, Forge vs OAuth tradeoffs, and Marketplace review timelines were not confirmed (admin support page failed; fetch budget ended).
